## Sync Pipeline v2 Research Programme — Phase 2a Model Swap Through Phase 4 Pre-Implementation (2026-08-04 to 2026-08-07)

Moved wholesale from `project-state.md`'s "Open Decisions" section during the 2026-08-09 docs
restructure (Phase 3) — this is the measurement-and-design research trail behind the v2
sync-pipeline timing-source upgrade (`docs/ws1-sync-pipeline/sync-pipeline-v2-plan.md`),
preserved verbatim here for a later pruning pass. No `src/` changes occurred anywhere in this
programme except a single comment correction in `whisper.rs`, called out below where it happens.

### Phase 2a — model swap (turbo)

**CODE COMPLETE, verdicts pending (updated 2026-08-05).** The Spanish-or-French corpus blocker is resolved (a `Spanish Project` folder now exists in the corpus directory with audio/script/scene-doc) and `ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin` is provisioned in `src-tauri/models/` (measured: 1,624,555,275 bytes on disk, ~2.1-2.2 GiB peak/resident during inference — H.9). `whisper.rs` now targets the turbo model with `-l auto`/stored-language, `--dtw base.en` dropped (was a no-op, model-specific preset name), `-np` dropped (stderr is now scanned for the auto-detected-language line, verified not to change stdout token output). `Project.language` (persisted, detected-once-then-sticky, user-overridable in Project Settings) and the H.4 `unsupported-language` guard (error-severity log entry + persistent dismissible banner) both ship. Determinism re-verified on turbo (PASS, both with the literal Phase 0 command and with the actual shipped `-l auto` flag — byte-identical MD5s across all four runs on a small English corpus file). `tsc`/`cargo check`/`vitest` (1281/1281) all clean; the Language settings UI and the full unsupported-language guard path (log entry + badge + banner) were smoke-tested live in the dev server.

**Step 5's real-corpus half is now done (2026-08-04/05): fresh turbo resync + `window.__transcriptInspector()` CSV pull for V6, 173-seg, and the Spanish project** (`docs/V6-Smear-Phase2a.csv`, `docs/173-Smear-Phase2a.csv`, `docs/Spanish-Smear-Phase2a.csv`). Analysis of those CSVs against the base.en baseline found:
- **A genuine ~9.7s content dropout on V6** (78.97–88.67s): turbo's transcript is entirely missing segments 27–29's text ("But something stayed in you. Small and permanent. A new understanding of what the night actually is."), which base.en captured cleanly. Confirmed by full-transcript search (turbo has zero occurrences of "stayed"/"permanent" anywhere). This is a model-swap ACCURACY regression, not an alignment failure — no boundary or timing fix can recover text the model never emitted. **Consequence: Phase 2b must measure whether large-v3 (non-turbo) also drops this passage — it is now a real accuracy candidate, not merely a reference ceiling.**
- **The 173-project's segment 1 (title card) and segment 13 (planted "blue monkey" string) are confirmed correct skips** — neither's text appears anywhere in the turbo transcript, same as they didn't in base.en.
- **173-project segment 112 ("Some don't emerge.") is a turbo-era regression** (this exact boundary was a verified-correct `control` at Phase 0 on base.en). Mechanism: turbo drops the word "Some" (base.en has it, turbo doesn't) on top of a pre-existing, model-independent normalization asymmetry (script-side "don't" expands to "do not" via `textNormalize.ts`'s whole-string contraction step; transcript-side Whisper always splits it into two sub-word tokens `don`+`'t`, which never re-triggers that expansion, in either model era) — with "Some" present, base.en's hole-tolerant run computation cleared the run-survival gate; without it, turbo's match (1 of 4 normalized words, longest run 1) most likely fails it. Presented as the most likely mechanism from token evidence, not verified by running the pipeline.
- **A recurring small-scale word-drop pattern beyond the single large V6 case** — turbo silently drops short words ("Three", "No", "afraid", "Fen's", part of "Thick", part of "Catachan") at several other boundaries in the cross-era diff. Read as a systemic accuracy trait on this corpus, not isolated incidents.
- **Turbo-era smear baseline recorded** (V6/173/Spanish, mirroring Phase 1b's base.en table). Notably 173's negative-smear fraction improves (23.6%→15.4%) while V6's is roughly flat (34.4%→33.6%) — not evidence the timing source improved; Phase 2b measures that properly.
- **`verification-baseline.csv` now carries 69 blank `phase-2a` verdict rows** (47 existing boundaries + 22 new sync-log-flagged candidates, cross-referenced word-text-keyed per K9) for the owner's ear. **Phase 0's correct-verdict count is 30 of 47 — phase-2a's gate is ≥30 correct once the owner fills the cells.**
- **The 173-project's scene doc has drifted to 175 bracket-tagged segments** (was 173 at Phase 0) — flagged, not resolved; re-verify the count before trusting any future "173-project, segment N" reference by position.

**Phase 2a — DONE (2026-08-05).** The owner's ear-listening pass over the original 47-boundary verification set landed: **38 correct, 5 word-shifted, 1 FAIL, 2 N/A (transcription loss, not a boundary failure), 1 unverified.** Against the 44 rows with a real placement verdict: **38/44 verified — Phase 0 30/47 → phase-2a 38/44, gate ("does not get worse than Phase 0") PASSED** (39/44 if the owner reclassifies `seasons than you || can count and` as correct rather than word-shifted; doesn't change the outcome). Net improvement: 9 of the original 11 ear-verified word-shift cases resolved (2 remain: `does the same || what the job`, `s youngest scout || a girl of`); all 5 of Part L's short-segment-run cases resolved. Three findings recorded (no code changed): (1) a new third failure class — `seasons than you || can count and` cuts cleanly at a real pause, but the narrator's pause disagrees with the script's segmentation; a timing-source upgrade will NOT fix it, added to Part L; (2) pairIdx-20 ("chitin thick enough") now places correctly in live production, but the pinned `syncTiming.test.ts` fixture is synthetic/frozen and still correctly locks the still-present code defect — fixture NOT updated, Phase 6b's scope does NOT shrink; (3) R10 — 2 seam-related regressions (`s youngest scout || a girl of` V6, and a newly-found `They're the worst` 173-seg case) plus 2 control regressions (`and fat-soaked moss || bound with sinew`, `when you report || but your hands`), below the systemic threshold, recheck-and-recorded per Part F, **no constant retuned**. A missing regression row (`They're the worst`, 173-seg segment 5-6 — never in the original 47, missed at Phase 0) was added as a phase-2a-only row, not backfilled to Phase 0.

**Spanish (Step 5) — run completed cleanly, boundary quality UNVERIFIED, written acceptance recorded.** 27 scene-doc segments, genuine Spanish narration confirmed; the turbo transcription completed with no abort/error (399 raw tokens, 36 dropped, 363 kept, 27 silences, 92.02s audio). No Spanish boundaries have been listened to or added to `verification-baseline.csv` — that requires a Spanish speaker's ear, which this session does not have. Accepted in writing at the plan's Stage 1 lock-gate entry, with an explicit reopening trigger (voided the moment any Spanish-specific normalization/alignment code ships in Phase 3b). French/Portuguese/German corpus material remains completely absent — same accepted-gap treatment, per H.8's dormant-rules allowance.

### Phase 2b — timing-source measurement

**DONE 2026-08-05. DECISION: DTW ABANDONED; Phase 3 = FORCED ALIGNMENT.**

The measurement script is committed (K8 satisfied): `scripts/measure-word-onset.py` + `scripts/measure-word-onset.md`, with per-pause raw output at `docs/measurements/phase2b-onset-{v6,173}-turbo-{raw,dtw}.csv`. Headlines:

- **DTW changes timestamps by EXACTLY 0.000000000s** — measured against a purpose-added no-DTW control (`-nfa` alone), over all 4,579 V6 and 2,080 173 tokens. DTW was verifiably enabled (stderr `dtw = 1`), not silently ignored. The decision did not come down to the median-error gate at all.
- **Mechanism (why no DTW preset on any model could win):** under `-ml 1` whisper emits **gapless** token spans — each token starts exactly where the previous ended (97.8% of V6 transitions, 93.4% of 173's) — so a pause is *structurally* absorbed into the following word's declared span. Measured consequence: a word's declared start sits a median of just **+0.038s from the pause's START** (vs −0.500s from its end, where the word is actually spoken). Error tracks pause duration across every bucket. V6 is 25.6% silence vs 173's 10.5%, which is exactly why V6 measures 0.500s median error and 173 measures 0.080s.
- **Word-onset error, shipped config (turbo raw):** V6 median 0.500s / p95 1.283s / 97.4% negative-smear; 173 median 0.080s / p95 0.497s / 68.0%. Wall-clock 834.9s for V6's 23.7min (1.70× realtime); `-nfa` costs ~25-33%. Timing has ≥5.7% run-to-run noise on this machine.
- **Phase 1b's provisional thresholds are now FINALIZED**: median ≤100ms **kept but demoted** (it passes 173, a project with known real boundary defects); **p95 ≤250ms promoted to primary** — the brief's "tail matters more than the median" hypothesis is CONFIRMED; negative-smear <1% **kept and re-scoped as a source-replacement test** (unreachable by refining Whisper timestamps, by the gapless mechanism); and a **new fourth threshold — zero-duration real-word tokens must be 0** (today 68 on V6, 44 on 173), which none of the original three could detect. Shipped config fails **7 of 8 readings**. NOTE: Phase 1b's inspector "smear" and Phase 2b's "word-onset error" are **different metrics with different denominators** and must never be compared directly (V6 reads 33.6% vs 97.4% negative — both correct).
- **Two Phase 2a findings corrected.** (1) V6's 9.7s content dropout is caused by **flash attention, not turbo's accuracy** — `-nfa` alone recovers all three sentences verbatim. (2) 173 segment 112: turbo does **not** drop the word "Some" — it emits it with a **zero-duration** timestamp (`443.82-443.82`), which `filterMalformedTokens` discards (`whisperService.ts:1315`). That moves segment 112 from "unfixable" to "fixed by Phase 3", since a real duration recovers it.
- **A documented "fact" was falsified:** "`-nfa` breaks stdout printing" — stated in the plan (twice), `docs/ws1-sync-pipeline/boundary-drift-investigation.md`, and `whisper.rs`'s own comment — is **false** on the bundled binary (4,639 clean bracketed lines measured). All four sites corrected. The Phase 3 cost estimate that flowed from it (JSON rewrite + progress-bar loss) was never required by `-nfa`.
- **Phase 3d (adaptive silence thresholds): SKIP** — recorded per that phase's own instruction. The −45dB threshold is not the binding constraint; the failure is entirely token-side.
- **NOT measured, explicitly:** large-v3 configs (c)/(d) were **skipped by owner decision** — the accuracy question (does non-turbo avoid the dropout / zero-duration tokens?) is **open and unmeasured**. Forced alignment's real-world accuracy on this corpus is also unverified locally.
- **Read-only honored:** no pipeline behaviour changed, no constant retuned, `docs/measurements/verification-baseline.csv` untouched. The only source edit is a comment correction in `whisper.rs` (`cargo check` clean).

**Stage 1 LOCK: NOT PASSED** at this point in the programme, blocking list: (a) smear thresholds unmet → needs Phase 3, and **sharpened by Phase 2b**: the blocker is not "smear is too high" but **"the timing source is of the wrong kind — gapless spans, plus silently deleted words"**; DTW is eliminated as a remedy; (b) non-English corpus — **PARTIALLY RESOLVED**, Spanish exists and runs cleanly but is unlistened (accepted in writing, reopens at Phase 3b); French/Portuguese/German still absent (accepted); (c) ~~3 short-segment-run boundaries not yet in the verification set~~ **RESOLVED 2026-08-04** — 5 added, satisfying Part L's ≥3 requirement; (d) Contract IN/1→2 not yet verified guarantee-by-guarantee; (e) cross-cutting regression checklist (D.-1) not yet run; (f) ~~Phase 2a's own 69-row verdict gate unfilled~~ **RESOLVED 2026-08-05** — owner's listening pass landed, gate passed (38/44, see Phase 2a entry above). Items (a)/(d)/(e) still blocked the Stage 1 lock itself at this point.

### Phase 3 — forced alignment: blockers, and Blocker 2's measurement

**Blockers 1/3 closed, Blocker 2 measured, GATE VERDICT PENDING OWNER DECISION (2026-08-05).** Blocker 1 (model/license: `wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53` bare confirmed pretrain-only/no CTC head; MMS-FA is CC-BY-NC-4.0, personal/testing use only; jonatasgrosman Apache-2.0 per-language fine-tunes and `nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` are the commercial candidates, Parakeet's CTC-extractability outside NeMo explicitly UNVERIFIED and not on the critical path) and Blocker 3 (architecture (A) confirmed — FA supplies timing only, Whisper transcript + Hirschberg alignment unchanged; both models now run per sync, so latency increases versus today, on top of Whisper turbo's own 834.9s/~2.2GiB) are both closed — with a correction folded into H.3 (the "language selects a romanization strategy" premise holds only for MMS-FA; the Stage 1 timing interface is shaped (language → model, vocab, decode strategy)).

Blocker 2 (measuring MMS-FA itself): the prior prototype session's `/tmp/phase3/` artifacts (tokens, emission, onset-error CSVs for both V6 and 173) **survived**, but the driver script did not — the exact K8 `/tmp`-loss pattern recurring one phase later. Rebuilt and committed: `scripts/measure-forced-alignment.py` + `.md` (reuses `measure-word-onset.py`'s `prepare`/`score`/`report` unchanged; a real neighbour-bleed bug in the per-segment windowing was found and fixed while validating it; a second real bug — a too-tight zero-padding window causing a CTC constraint violation on one V6 segment — was handled by skipping that segment and continuing, matching this codebase's own established graceful-degradation philosophy). A fresh, honestly-timed run replaced the recovered run's implausible 3.4s `elapsed_sec` with real numbers: **full V6 (1421.3s audio) took 349.5s wall-clock (≈4.07× realtime — faster than Whisper turbo's own 1.70×) at 4.01 GiB peak RSS; 173 took 112.7s at 3.98 GiB peak RSS** (peak RSS is dominated by model weights, not audio length). Combined architecture-(A) cost: Whisper (834.9s) + FA (349.5s) = 1184.4s total, a **41.9% latency increase** over today's Whisper-only pipeline; memory is `max(~2.1–2.2 GiB, 4.01 GiB) ≈ 4.01 GiB`, not the sum, if the two stages run sequentially with memory released between them.

Four-threshold table result: **3 of 8 readings fail** (median passes both projects; p95 — the primary reading — passes 173 (69.9ms) but fails V6 at 476ms vs. the 250ms gate; negative-smear fails both; zero-duration tokens pass both, cleanly resolving Phase 2b's Finding 4). This is a large improvement over Whisper turbo's 7-of-8 fail, not a clean pass.

**The ratio analysis the owner asked for (Part L's governing relation, applied to every V6 >250ms failure) is the real finding, and it is stronger than a first pass suggested.** Of 61 V6 failures, only 6 exceed severity ratio 0.5 and only 2 exceed ratio 1.0 (V6 segment 144 "Wind.", the confirmed Whisper defect, sits at ratio ≈1.0 for calibration — and IS one of the two). Cross-referencing every ratio>0.5 row against FA's own per-word confidence score (which this measurement captures and Whisper's own output has no equivalent of) found **zero of the six are cases where FA was confident AND wrong**: 3 are the "it"-word scorer artifact (FA confidence 0.94–1.00 — it wasn't confused, the SCORING method misattributed the word to the wrong pause); 3 are cases FA itself flags as low-confidence (score 0.01–0.05), and 2 of those 3 land exactly on segments already catalogued as pre-existing base.en-era Whisper timing defects (segment 61 = word-shift-11's "not hard" case; segment 144 = Part L's own governing-ratio example) — because this measurement's zero-padding window (a direct consequence of the corpus being perfectly gapless, Key Invariant (f)) is exactly that already-wrong committed span, FA is correctly flagging that it can't find real audio in a window that may not contain it. No cascade-class failure exists anywhere in FA's V6 output. Separately, the "4 of 50 are the scorer's own midpoint edge case" claim was checked directly against the data: **the true count is 8, not 4** — all the word "it.", all FA-confidence ≥0.94, all the same mechanism (a very short word's midpoint barely crosses the pause-start selection threshold); a ~12ms margin cutoff happens to yield exactly 4, but all 8 share one mechanism. A related, evidence-based finding on the negative-smear threshold: FA's negative errors are tiny in magnitude (90th-percentile ~25–39ms on both projects) — nothing like Whisper's whole-pause-absorption pattern — so a genuinely non-gapless source can still fail the literal "<1%" gate; this is a measured correction to Phase 2b's assumption about that metric, not a proposal to retune the number. One V6 segment (320, a 102-character sentence in a 1.27s slot) failed to align entirely under the zero-padding window and was skipped, not crashed — itself evidence that "committed duration, zero padding" cannot be the real production windowing strategy.

**Per explicit instruction, no threshold was retuned and no gate was self-certified.** The 250ms figure was a provisional judgment call, never independently derived; the gate verdict — pass Stage 1's timing-source item as measured, or revise the p95 threshold on this evidence, or something else — was left for the owner. Integration (Rust inference path, Viterbi, model provisioning) had **not** been started and did not start until the owner decided.

**Phase 3 follow-up (2026-08-05) — two measurement-only tasks, no integration, no threshold retuned.**

*Task 1 — harness-artifact hypothesis, CONFIRMED for all 5 of 5 low-confidence V6 rows tested.* Corrected an earlier prose-summary miscount: of the 6 V6 rows at severity ratio>0.5, only 1 (segment 171, "it.") is the it-scorer artifact — the other 5 (segment 61 ×2 words, 144, 80, 303) are the low-FA-confidence rows. Re-measured all 5 with padding widened to ±1.5s and the neighbour-midpoint clamp bypassed (a diagnostic-only bypass via a direct library call into `measure-forced-alignment.py`'s own `align_segment()` — the committed script's default padding/clamp behaviour is untouched). 3 resolved cleanly (near-zero error, ~1.0 confidence); 2 (144, 80) got WORSE under the naive wide-window bypass — root-caused as `with_star` neighbour-bleed (confirmed: segment 80's re-aligned "No" landed inside segment 79's own committed span), not a real FA defect, since both segments sit in perfectly gapless runs where the neighbour-midpoint clamp already equals their own committed boundary (zero legal padding room). A second method — one joint MMS-FA pass per 5-segment group with the full correct multi-segment text, removing the neighbour-bleed confound entirely — resolved both remaining cases cleanly too (144: err +0.038s/conf 0.911; 80: err +0.019s/conf 0.995, correctly disambiguated from segment 79's own earlier "No"). **All 5 confirmed: FA was correctly refusing on a window that didn't contain the true audio, not producing a confident wrong answer.** Recomputed V6 p95 with the 4 affected segments' tokens spliced into the full 502-pause dataset: 476.2ms→442.2ms — **still fails the 250ms gate**, because p95 is dominated by ~55 other >250ms rows this diagnostic didn't touch (the already-documented 8-occurrence "it." scorer-artifact cluster, plus the still-open ~42-case high-confidence/large-margin cluster). Two independent methods (severity-ratio classification, targeted re-measurement) now agree on every boundary either has examined; neither claims to have explained the rest.

*Task 2 — commercial-license de-risking: jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-english (Apache-2.0) verified viable, numerically within noise of MMS-FA.* Verified before measuring (not assumed): real `Wav2Vec2ForCTC` architecture + 33-symbol vocab (unlike the bare Meta pretrain checkpoint Blocker 1 already ruled out), weight blob exactly 1,261,942,732 bytes, and a live greedy-decode sanity check against project 173's own audio producing accurate transcription. Measured on 173 via a new committed script (`scripts/measure-forced-alignment-hf.py` + `.md`, same K8 discipline, reuses `measure-word-onset.py`'s scoring unchanged): median 27.5ms / p95 89.7ms / negative-smear 44.8% / 0 zero-duration tokens — both gate-passing readings (median, p95) within 5–20ms of MMS-FA's own 22.3ms/69.9ms on the same project, negative-smear fails for the same already-documented reason MMS-FA's does. Cost: ~28% slower wall-clock (143.97s vs 112.7s), but ~20% LESS peak RSS (3.19 GiB vs 3.98 GiB) — no multilingual/romanizer overhead. Real trade-offs, stated plainly: ~1.2GB model **per language** (≈6GB for H.0's five languages, vs. MMS-FA's one multilingual ~1.2GB checkpoint, only English measured so far), and no digit-reading capability (degrades, doesn't drop, e.g. "41st"→"st"). **Consequence: the commercial path is viable; Parakeet's unverified CTC-extractability does not need investigating unless this candidate is rejected on the multi-language footprint or an unmeasured non-English accuracy gap.**

### Phase 3 data-cleaning pass (2026-08-05)

Four steps, measurement-only, no threshold retuned, no integration started. Three new committed scripts: `measure-forced-alignment-joint-context.py`, `measure-forced-alignment-whisper-text.py`, `extract-full-transcript.py` (+ `scripts/phase3-data-cleaning.md`).

**Step 1 fixed the "it." scorer bug** in `measure-word-onset.py`'s `score_onset_errors` — its midpoint-only "following word" test didn't scale with token duration, so a very short sentence-final word's ordinary trailing edge-blur could cross the threshold and get misattributed to the pause AFTER it. Added an overlap gate (candidate must reach the silence's own midpoint, not just poke past its start). Re-scored the full V6 dataset: 490/502 rows byte-identical (zero regressions), 12 rows fixed (not just the known 8 "it." cases — also "hard.", "Yaro", "temporary.", "right.", sharing the identical mechanism). One consequence worth flagging: segment 61's "hard." — the single HIGHEST severity-ratio row in the whole V6 dataset (1.356) — turns out to be entirely this scorer bug, not the low-FA-confidence issue previously believed.

**Step 2 re-measured the remaining 49 (61 minus Step 1's 12) raw >250ms V6 failures** via joint multi-segment context (Method 2 only, not Method 1's wide-padding bypass, per instruction) — 29 merged windows, 139.5s wall-clock. **9 of 49 resolved cleanly** (confirmed harness artifacts of the zero-padding window — includes re-confirming segments 144/80 already published, plus 7 new ones). **40 of 49 remain unresolved**, moved by <30ms despite full context and high confidence on both passes — reported as genuinely still-failing per instruction, not softened. New observation: all 40 share the same sign (FA places the word LATER than `silencedetect`'s pause end, 0.28–2.1s) and cluster on sentence-initial pronouns — consistent with, but not proof of, an open "real micro-pause/breath" hypothesis.

**Step 3 recomputed the V6 gate number with Steps 1+2 applied:** median 21.2ms→**19.7ms** (passes ≤100ms), **p95 476ms→338.2ms (still fails the 250ms gate)**, negative-smear 49.0%→46.9% (still fails <1%). **40 genuine unresolved >250ms failures remain.**

**Step 4, a separate arm, not folded into the Step 3 gate number.** WER/CER classification (computed first, before any FA run): naive word-level WER is unusable for 173/Spanish (24.8%/86.3%, both Whisper sub-word-tokenization artifacts, not drift) — substituted character-level CER: V6 4.4%, 173 2.2%, Spanish 5.5% (raw CER >5%, but traced directly to two non-drift writing-convention patterns — "Scylla"→"Silla," "seis"/"tres"→"6"/"3" — not content divergence). **All three projects classify faithful.** Then ran script-text mode vs. whisper-text mode FA on the faithful subset (V6+173 only — Spanish excluded, no persisted per-segment timing backup, declined to reconstruct): on verified-faithful content, script-text mode beats whisper-text mode on every reading but negative-smear (median 6.0x/1.7x better, p95 1.9x/7.5x better, low-confidence rate 6.2x/4.5x lower, on V6/173) and whisper-text mode structurally cannot align any segment Whisper transcribed nothing for (3 such V6 segments). **Confirms the instructed design: whisper-text mode stays the drifted-audio fallback, not a general default.**

**Gate verdict: still left to the owner, per explicit instruction.** The apples-to-apples number against the MMS-FA baseline is Step 3's: **p95 338.2ms, still above the 250ms gate, with 40 confirmed-genuine remaining failures** (down from 61 raw / 476ms, but not a pass). Step 4's script-text-mode finding is a candidate improvement to the eventual production windowing strategy (align against script text on faithful content), not evidence bearing on whether Stage 1's timing-source item passes as measured.

### Phase 3 reference-validity pass (2026-08-05)

Four steps, measurement-only, no threshold retuned. Task: test, not assume, the hypothesis that the 40 unresolved failures' uniform sign (FA always later than `silencedetect`, never earlier) means the REFERENCE is biased, not FA. Three new committed scripts: `phase3-reference-validity-step-{a,b,c}-*.py` (+ `scripts/phase3-reference-validity.md`).

**Step A (threshold sweep) — CONFIRMED for 34 of 40, REFUTED for 6 of 40.** Re-ran `silencedetect` on V6 at -50/-45/-40/-35/-30dB. Median \|error\| across the 40 collapses **365.6ms→17.7ms** (~20x) between -45 and -35dB — a more permissive floor lets the detected silence extend further into a soft onset ramp, pushing the declared pause end later, toward where FA (and the true audio) actually place the word. **34/40 (85%) drop under 50ms by -35 or -30dB.** But **6/40 are flat across the entire sweep** (segments 383/307/1/224/42 "You", 442 "They" — errors 1452/2139/1004/369/330/321ms, unchanged at every floor including the most permissive -30dB tested) — for these, the bias hypothesis is dead; whatever's wrong isn't a fixed-floor artifact. p95 barely moves (1004ms→985ms) because it's dominated by exactly these 6 outliers. **Net: the 40-count is no longer a uniform population — 6, not 40, are the residual genuine-failure set.** Full table: `docs/measurements/phase3-step-a-threshold-sweep.csv`.

**Step B (phonetic class) — large soft-vs-sharp gap, supports Step A's mechanism.** All 501 V6 boundaries bucketed by CMU-dict first-phoneme class. Soft onsets (vowel/glide/nasal/liquid) read p95 368.3ms / 10.3% >250ms; sharp (plosive/fricative/affricate) read p95 248.2ms / 4.9%. Sharper still fine-grained: **plosive and affricate both read a clean 0.0% >250ms corpus-wide**, while **glide (mostly "You"/"Your"/"When") reads 14.1% >250ms**, the worst bucket. Among the 40 unresolved failures: 30/40 soft, 10/40 sharp — **and every one of the 10 sharp cases is a fricative; zero are plosive or affricate**, exactly the two classes that read 0% everywhere else in the corpus. Full table: `docs/measurements/phase3-step-b-phoneme-bucket.csv`.

**Step C (real ground truth) — SCORED 2026-08-06.** 8 from the 40 unresolved (4 of Step A's flat outliers, 2 that resolve by -35dB, 2 mid-range) + 4 passing controls, 1.0s-padded, opaque `clip_01`–`clip_12` naming, manifest carries script text only. The owner's returned A/breath/B labels for all 12 clips were scored against the private answer key. Headlines:

- **C1 (integrity):** 9/12 clips matched the 1.0s pad point as expected. Of the 3 that didn't, clip 3 (segment 1, the file's very first segment) is **excluded** — the human's reported boundary describes a different sentence pause than the one the pipeline flagged, and FA's own token span for that segment is independently anomalous (1.87s for one word). Clips 10/11 (segments 383/307) are **retained** — silencedetect anchored to a stale, earlier pause in the same multi-pause clip, but FA's onset call corroborates the human's true boundary to within 39ms/335ms, so the human and FA are demonstrably describing the same event.
- **C2 (three-way score, n=7 scored failures + 4 controls):** **FA is closer to human than silencedetect on all 7 scored failures**, by 6x-78x (median ~15x). FA error: 12.3-38.6ms on 6 of 7; silencedetect error: 335.5-2473.9ms on all 7. **Stated directly: the 40 unresolved Phase 3 failures were never predominantly FA errors — they were failures of a biased reference.** One exception stated just as directly: clip 11/segment 307 leaves FA itself 335.2ms off true ground truth.
- **C3 (breath mechanism) — CONFIRMED with direct evidence, count-corrected.** 6 clips have audible breath (not 7, a correction to this pass's own assumption), all 6 with breath ending 63-139ms before human B. **silencedetect's declared pause-end lands within 3ms of breath ONSET on 4 of 5 scorable breath clips** (0.19-2.75ms) — it is measuring the breath, not the word. The 6 no-breath clips split sharply: the 4 controls are near-exact (0.7-4.6ms); the 2 no-breath failures (both threshold-invariant residuals) are off by 1413ms/2474ms for an unrelated reason (stale-pause selection, C1) — a three-way split, not the simple two-way one hypothesized, but still the strongest available confirmation that breath bias is real and separately bounded from the residual mechanism.
- **C4 (threshold-invariant residuals):** 4 of the 6 (segments 383, 307, 1, 442) are in this sample; segments 224/42 are not and remain entirely unexamined. Of the 4: segment 442 fully resolves (breath-driven reference bias, FA accurate to 14ms); segment 383 fully resolves (stale-pause reference bias, FA accurate to 39ms); segment 307 partially resolves (same reference bias, but FA itself still off by 335ms); segment 1 is uncharacterizable (excluded, C1).
- **C5 (gate number):** n=11 scored clips is explicitly **not enough to set or extrapolate a corpus p95** — reported as a sample, not a corpus figure. Failures (n=7): FA median 24.6ms / p95 246.2ms; silencedetect median 434.2ms / p95 2155.7ms. 6 of 7 scored failures pass the 250ms gate against human truth; 1 (segment 307) fails at 335.2ms.

**Bottom line, C1-C5:** against human ground truth, FA looks accurate enough to be a real timing-source candidate (12-39ms error on 6 of 7 scored failures, indistinguishable from its own control-set noise), and `silencedetect` looks unfit to remain the sole scoring reference for this kind of boundary (335-2474ms error on the same 7, with a confirmed breath-onset bias mechanism). This is a 12-clip sample, not a corpus-wide verdict.

**Step D (negative-smear audit) — no computation inconsistency found; the <1% GATE is the wrong shape, not the arithmetic.** `negative_smear_fraction` and p95 come from the identical `errors` list, identical population, identical `silences.json` reference, inside one function call — verified directly: of the corrected 501-row V6 dataset, 235 rows (46.9%, matches Step 3 exactly) are negative-sign, of which 234 (99.6%) are sub-50ms noise and **zero** exceed 250ms. The 40 unresolved failures are a disjoint, magnitude-selected positive-only tail of the same distribution — a row cannot be in both sets by construction. A source with accurate, symmetric-around-zero noise will always read ~50% negative-smear by this literal sign-only definition, regardless of how good it actually is; the <1% gate was built to catch Whisper's whole-pause-absorption pathology (~500ms median negative smear) and cannot structurally be passed by an accurate-but-noisy source.

**Provenance dig (git-verified, not inferred):** all four thresholds trace to commit `c522248`, written as "provisional until Phase 2b measures it" while Phase 1b/2b were both still NOT STARTED per that same commit's own status table — an author judgment call predating any local measurement, not a fit to data. The reference METHOD (`silencedetect` vs. declared word start) is older still, from the original `/tmp`-lost investigation that produced the ~190ms figure (K8, confirmed unrecoverable) — but `silencedetect` has been the SOLE reference across every phase; only the candidate under test has changed (Whisper base.en → turbo → DTW → now FA). The gate was never "measuring against Whisper timestamps instead of silencedetect" — this reference-validity question had simply never been asked by any prior phase before this pass.

**Verdict, stated plainly (updated 2026-08-06 — Step C returned a verdict):** the 250ms gate had been measuring a mix of both reference bias and real timing behavior, not FA accuracy cleanly — Step A shows 34 of the 40 "failures" are an artifact of a fixed -45dB floor exiting a soft onset early, not a defect in FA's placement, and Step C's human-labeled 12-clip sample confirms this directly: FA is closer to human truth than silencedetect on all 7 scored failures (12-39ms vs. 335-2474ms on 6 of 7), and silencedetect's declared pause-end lands within 3ms of breath onset on 4 of 5 scorable breath clips. Per explicit instruction, no threshold was retuned — the sample is too small (n=11 scored clips) to set a corpus p95.

### Phase 3 reference-correction pass (2026-08-06), Steps E-H

Measurement only, no threshold retuned. Task: fix the scoring reference itself (not FA), since Step C already showed FA tracking human to 12-39ms on 6 of 7 failures while silencedetect was biased 335-2474ms. Three new committed scripts: `scripts/phase3-stale-pause-audit.py`, `scripts/phase3-breath-aware-reference.py`, `scripts/phase3-step-h-fresh-batch-clips.py`.

**Step E (stale-pause selection audit, all 446 real V6 boundaries — audited, not assumed).** Defined the harness's actual selection rule (`score_onset_errors`'s ordinal greedy walk, no distance cap, no boundary-plausibility check) and audited every real boundary against FA's own (human-validated) word onsets. **The walk is correct for 418/440 (95%); wrong for only 5 corpus-wide, and all 5 are already-known Step-2 zero-padding artifacts — zero of the 40 unresolved failures show a fixable selection-rule bug.** Exactly 3 of the 40 (segments 1, 307, 383) are a genuine DETECTOR-COVERAGE GAP, not a selection bug — no closer silence was ever independently detected anywhere in the corpus near their true onsets (confirmed independently by Step A's flat -50dB→-30dB sweep on these same 3). A distance-cap fix (reject an attribution beyond 1.0s, informed by the clean population's own p99 ~530ms, not fit to the outliers) excludes these 3 and moves p95 338.2ms→331.3ms, n>250ms 40→37 — small, honest movement, not the pervasive bug the working hypothesis worried about. **Answer to the count asked for: 3 of 40, not "large and embarrassing" — smaller than expected.**

**Step F (breath-aware corrected reference, built on acoustic principle, thresholds fixed before any human comparison).** Four frame-level features (32ms/8ms Hann windows) separate breath from silence from voiced onset: file-adaptive RMS-dB bands (p10/p60 percentiles, not a fixed dB value), spectral flatness (Wiener entropy, 150-4000Hz band; breath ≈ noise-like/high, voiced ≈ tonal/low), zero-crossing rate, and harmonicity (peak normalized autocorrelation, 70-350Hz pitch range). Thresholds (flatness 0.35, harmonicity 0.35/0.5) are standard-literature round numbers, not corpus-fit. **Disclosed plainly:** this session had already read Step C's published aggregate findings before designing the detector — full blindness on the ORIGINAL 12 can't be claimed, only that specific threshold values weren't reverse-fit to them and weren't adjusted after seeing the comparison. One genuine implementation bug (a search-window scope error, not a threshold) was found and fixed via an internal check unrelated to the human labels. **Result on the 12 known clips (informational, not blind):** breath correctly detected on 5/6 true-breath clips (1 false positive on a control, disclosed, still under-gate); corrected onsets on the 5 real breath failures improve from 335-512ms to 1-232ms against human B, clearing the 250ms gate on all 5. **Result on the full 40 unresolved failures: breath detected in exactly 37/40 — precisely the 37 NOT flagged by Step E — and 35/40 total now resolve to ≤250ms.** The remaining 5 = Step E's 3 detector-misses + 2 (segments 224, 42) showing no breath signal at all, unresponsive to this correction, still entirely unexamined by any ground truth.

**Step G (segment 307 / clip 11, the one confirmed genuine FA residual — investigated, not generalized).** FA places "You" ("You are forty-nine.") at 929.335s (conf. 0.9838), 335ms before human B (929.670s); neither Step E nor Step F touches it (no closer candidate exists at all). Frame-level acoustic inspection found NOT a soft-glide ramp but ~4.8s of substantial, clearly-voiced acoustic activity (924.77-929.34s) between the preceding segment's declared end and FA's placement of "You" — matching NEITHER adjacent segment's script text. The raw turbo Whisper transcript for this window reads **"Level 8 The one who teaches what cannot be taught easily"** — almost certainly a spoken heading/chapter-marker (the file's own first words are "Level one") interposed in the recording with no script representation. Whisper's own raw transcript already places "You" at 929.330 — essentially identical to FA's 929.335, both ~340ms early — because FA's search window inherits Whisper's own (wrong) token position via the unchanged Hirschberg alignment, reproducing rather than correcting the error. **A genuine, distinct, one-off defect — not the soft-onset-pronoun pattern the other 37 share — explicitly not generalized to segments 1/383 or any broader class.**

**Step H (corpus re-score + fresh confirmation batch).** V6 corpus, before vs. after Steps E+F: median 19.7ms→18.3ms (unchanged, was never the failing reading); **p95 338.2ms→82.2ms — a 4x improvement, now comfortably inside the 250ms gate**; negative-smear 46.9%→50.8% (still fails the literal <1% gate, unchanged verdict — Step D already established this metric structurally cannot discriminate an accurate-but-noisy source); **boundaries >250ms: 40→2** (segments 42 and 224 — both unexplained, both unresponsive to breath correction, small enough now to name individually). **Provisional** — rests on a reference validated only against the original, non-blind-checked 12 clips. A fresh, non-overlapping 20-clip batch was exported to confirm: 12 from the current worst-remaining residuals (including both boundaries still >250ms), 8 phonetically-varied controls, none reusing any of the original 12's segments. Same 1.0s-padding protocol as Step C, opaque `clip2_01`-`clip2_20` names. **Padding/duration verified programmatically for all 20 before export — every clip's pre/post padding measured exactly 1.000s and every file's actual duration matched expected to <5ms, all 20 PASS** (the prior batch's 3 unexplained offsets do not recur).

### Blinded-batch scoring pass (2026-08-06), Steps I-L

Measurement only, no threshold retuned. One new committed script: `scripts/phase3-step-i-l-audit.py` (four subcommands: `extract-raw-transcript`, `transcript-audit`, `heading-sweep`, `score-batch2`).

**Step I (export integrity audit, run first per instruction).** Clip 11's mismatch (segment 321, "That") is **not** an export-path bug — root-caused to an upstream FA-alignment cascade: segment 320 is confirmed, by a zero-FA-token sweep, to be the **only segment in the entire 447-segment V6 corpus with zero aligned tokens** (the already-known CTC-constraint-violation skip from Blocker 2). The full, untruncated raw transcript shows segment 320's real content — 102 characters — genuinely spoken across ~5.8s (973.9-979.7s), crammed into a committed slot of only 1.27s (a 4.5x undercount, pre-dating Phase 3). Deprived of a valid neighbour boundary, segment 321's own windowed FA search misplaced "That" ~4s early, into what is actually segment 320's own unrecovered speech. **This defect was invisible to every numeric gate** — segment 321's onset error against silencedetect was 227ms, under the 250ms gate, in both the original and the Steps-E+F-corrected datasets, since it was never in the original 40-failure list; only the human listener caught it. A reproducible check of all 32 clips confirms **only clip2_11 is a genuine content mismatch** — 3 other raw prefix-test flags (clip_10/seg383, clip_11/seg307, clip2_02/seg224) are the SAME benign, already-explained pattern Step K formalizes (a heading recitation precedes the flagged word, so the segment's real content sits later in the clip than a naive prefix test expects, but it IS present and correct). **Consequence for C1-C5: none** — neither segment 320 nor 321 appears in the original 12-clip batch, and the zero-token sweep confirms segment 320 is uniquely responsible; the FA-tracks-human finding is unaffected.

**Step J (score the 17 valid clips — excludes clip 11 per Step I, clips 9/15 held aside per instruction).** Scored FA onset, raw silencedetect, and a fresh run of the already-committed breath-aware reference (Step F's method, applied for the first time to genuinely unseen material) against human B. **Two catastrophic outliers dominate the aggregate** — clip2_02/seg224 (FA −882ms) and clip2_12/seg42 (FA −1298ms) — both independently confirmed in Step K to be the heading-recitation class, not fresh FA failures. **Excluding those two, FA's worst error across the remaining 15 clips is 131.6ms** — comfortably under the 250ms gate. Breath vs. no-breath (n=6/11): FA median 14.9ms/28.3ms, silencedetect median 221.1ms/3.1ms — the breath bias is confirmed as the dominant no-breath-vs-breath split. **The Step F corrected reference does NOT hold up as an unqualified improvement on this genuinely blind batch** — on 8 of 17 rows its error exceeds raw silencedetect's (occasionally firing past the true onset into ordinary trailing-consonant energy on a clean control), though it remains a clear net win specifically on breath clips (median 94.0ms vs. SD's 221.1ms).

**Step K (unscripted spoken headings, treated as a class).** A full-transcript sweep for the literal token "Level" (V6's chapter-marker convention) finds **exactly 10 occurrences, one per chapter, all absent from every segment's script text** — not 3 (the count this investigation had accumulated incidentally). All 10 sit precisely at a chapter boundary, consuming 2.79-5.58s (median ~4.2s) of dead-to-the-script audio that the current pipeline **splits arbitrarily between the two neighbouring segments**, at whatever point a stale/spurious silencedetect interval happens to land inside the recitation (verified on 4 sampled cases: 47-92% of the heading's duration lands on the PRECEDING segment, the rest on the following one). **Consequence for FA: it has nothing to align to during a heading** (neither neighbour's script text occurs there), so the boundary is decided entirely by silencedetect's own candidates — typically internal pauses WITHIN the heading — producing a cut at an essentially arbitrary point inside unscripted content that corrupts both neighbours' on-screen timing in a way word-onset-only scoring cannot see. Clips 9 (segment 264) and 15 (segment 293), held aside pending this step, are **confirmed NOT the same class**: clip 9 is an ordinary stale-pause-selection instance on a genuinely tiny (~60ms) true gap; clip 15 is a well-behaved breath case with an ordinary perceptual A-endpoint ambiguity. A bounded keyword sweep of the 173-project and Spanish-project full transcripts found no chapter-marker vocabulary in either (173's 2 hits — "squad level", "familiar part ends" — are ordinary in-sentence usage) — **this defect class appears V6-specific** (its narration alone uses a chapter convention), though this was not an exhaustive script-vs-transcript diff for the other two projects.

**Step L (segments 42 and 224).** **Both appear in this batch** (224 = clip2_02, 42 = clip2_12) and are now **fully explained, not merely re-confirmed as unexplained**: both are the two most severe examples of the Step K heading-recitation class.

**Bottom line for I-L, stated plainly:** the export path itself is clean (verified across all 32 clips) except for one genuine, disclosed, structurally-isolated FA-cascade defect (segment 321, caused by segment 320's pre-existing 4.5x duration undercount) that never touched any prior conclusion. Excluding that one clip and the two now-explained heading-contaminated residuals (42, 224), FA's worst error against real human ground truth on this GENUINELY BLIND batch is 131.6ms — the corrected reference survives on the material it was never fitted to. The Step F breath-aware reference is a real but qualified improvement (a clear win on breath clips, an occasional regression on clean controls) — not the clean unconditional win the original 12-clip check suggested.

### Phase 3 → Phase 4 handoff (2026-08-06), Steps M-P

Baseline capture only, per explicit instruction: no Rust changes, no timing-source swap, no Viterbi, no contract amendment. Purpose: freeze a reproducible pre-implementation baseline so a future swap can be judged per-boundary against what ships today, not just in aggregate.

**Step M (golden baseline).** A new vitest harness (`scripts/phase4-handoff-replay-sync.test.ts`) replays the real, unmodified, currently-shipped Apply-Sync pipeline — `App.tsx`'s `cachedTokensReady` branch and `useWhisper.ts`'s `alignSegmentsFromCachedTranscript`, called in their exact production sequence, zero reimplementation — against each project's own scene doc/script and the already-captured turbo Whisper tokens (unchanged since Phase 2a Step 5). One disclosed substitution: production's silence source (`silenceDetector.ts`'s Web-Audio RMS scan, browser-only) was re-implemented line-for-line in Python (`scripts/phase4-handoff-app-silence.py`) against the same 16kHz transcode, since ffmpeg's `silencedetect` (used elsewhere in this document as an independent scoring reference) is a *different* algorithm and would have snapped against the wrong silence source. All three projects reproduced cleanly (444/447, 172/175, 26/27 kept; zero gate aborts) and the replay independently re-derived three already-published findings without being told the answer first — V6's segments 27-29 dropout, 173's segment-1/13 skips, and, notably, **173 segment 112's turbo-era regression, which Phase 2b had only hypothesized from token evidence and this replay now directly confirms by running the real pipeline.** Key Invariant (b) (committed duration = audioDuration) holds exactly on all three. Committed: `docs/phase4-baseline-{v6,173,spanish}-{segments,words,skipped,silences}.csv` + `docs/measurements/phase4-baseline-methodology.md` (full provenance: commit `c4fc289`, `ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin`, ffmpeg 8.1.1-tessus, Intel i9-9980HK/macOS 26.5.2, no GPU). Spanish has no persisted post-sync backup to diff against (already-known gap) — this pass reconstructed it via the same real-code replay rather than reusing an independent snapshot, disclosed as a narrower but real residual gap, not hidden.

**Step N (closing the two measurement gaps).** N.1 — MMS-FA run on Spanish for the first time (it was the original reason for Phase 2a and had never been measured): median 61.2ms ✓, p95 282.1ms ✗ (misses the 250ms gate narrowly, on a 22-pause sample — well within plausible sampling noise), negative-smear 9.1% ✗ (expected structurally, per Step D), zero-duration tokens 0 ✓ — 2 of 4 pass, no cascade failures, favorable but a small, still-unlistened sample; the Stage 1 written acceptance for Spanish is unchanged. One new finding: MMS-FA also can't romanize digits (`uroman` drops "12"), the same limitation already documented for jonatasgrosman on English, now confirmed on MMS-FA and on a non-English project. N.2 — jonatasgrosman run on V6 (median 25.8ms, p95 400.8ms — within noise of MMS-FA's 21.2ms/476ms, and **both models fail on the identical V6 segment, 320**, independently confirming that defect is a pre-existing committed-duration bug, not an aligner artifact) and on Spanish (result: median 61.2ms / p95 282.1ms / negative-smear 9.1% / 0 zero-duration tokens — **numerically identical to MMS-FA's own Spanish numbers to 1 decimal place**, verified as genuine convergence, not a scoring-script bug re-reading the same file). Spanish's jonatasgrosman weights (~1.18GiB) required a cold download that stalled repeatedly on this session's network across three automated attempts; the user completed the download manually and the file was wired into the local HF cache and run offline.

**Step O (known-defect inventory, 12 classes, spec only).** Every defect class surfaced across all of Phase 3 enumerated with instance counts, affected projects, whether any of the four numeric gates would catch it, and a specified (unimplemented) structural check: zero-aligned-token/CTC-violation segments (1, V6 seg 320 — invisible to the onset-error gate, caused the segment-321 cascade); unscripted spoken headings (10, V6-only "Level N" convention); stale-pause/detector-coverage gaps (3, V6); breath-vs-boundary misclassification (dominant mechanism on V6, unresolved as an unconditional fix); the already-fixed "it." scorer bug (measurement-tool only); the flash-attention content dropout (V6 segs 27-29); 173 segment 112 (now closed — the run-survival gate works as intended); systemic small word-drops; the CTC-violation integration-design gap; the 3 residual word-shift cases (1 structurally unfixable by any timing-source upgrade); the confirmed-broken lock-preservation bug (K13, unrelated to timing, a Stage 3 concern); and the negative-smear gate itself, shown analytically incapable of passing ANY accurate source, not a pipeline defect.

**Step P (cost and rollback).** Whisper-only wall-clock re-grounded per project rather than citing V6's figure alone: V6 834.9s (1.70×RT), 173 452.3s (1.57×RT), Spanish **108.5s/2.18GiB peak RSS, measured fresh this pass** (0.85×RT — a short clip pays Whisper's fixed model-load cost disproportionately). Alignment+snap is sub-second on all three combined (Step M's own harness ran all 3 in 3.69s). Adding a forced-alignment pass costs **+41.9% on V6, +24.9% on 173, +18.3% on Spanish** — project-size-dependent, not a universal "+42%." Peak RSS is not additive (sequential models); the practical floor rises from ~2.1-2.2GiB to ~3.2-4.0GiB regardless of which candidate model ships. Reversibility: only Stage 1's per-token timestamp VALUES are replaced (the `{text,start,end}` contract is unchanged); Whisper's transcript, Hirschberg alignment, and every downstream stage are untouched; old/new can run side-by-side today in measurement and architecturally in production via a capability-gate pattern this codebase already ships elsewhere (`useExport.ts`'s `isWebCodecsExportGateOpen()`); rollback is "skip the FA pass," no schema change.

### Phase 4 pre-implementation (2026-08-06), Steps Q-T

No `src/` changes, no production Rust, no threshold retuned. Six owner decisions recorded verbatim — most consequentially: **MMS-FA is now permanently OUT** (decision 3 — `jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53`, all 5 languages, is the permanent standard; MMS-FA's CC-BY-NC-4.0 license never ships, not even temporarily), and **the 250ms p95 gate is now APPROVED** (decision 1). **The stated tension is real and unresolved by this pass on purpose: Spanish's p95 (282.1ms) fails the now-approved 250ms gate**, by 32.1ms on a 22-pause sample — Step Q tests whether that's reference bias (as English turned out to be) or genuine FA error, not prejudged either way.

**Step Q — 10 blinded Spanish clips exported and integrity-checked, ready to send.** 7 from the worst-scoring MMS-FA boundaries, 3 controls, same 1.0s-padding protocol as both English batches. **Programmatic integrity check (run BEFORE sending, per instruction, using the production whisper-cli sidecar) — 10/10 pass all three tests** (first-word present, lead-in matches the previous segment's tail, no foreign content). One qualified pass disclosed, not hidden: clip3_06's first word "Scylla" is heard as "Silla" — the same documented ASR writing convention from Step 4's CER analysis, not a content error. One structural risk flagged without naming the clip: one failure clip sits at the corpus's very start, the same edge-of-corpus condition that forced batch 1's clip 3 out of scoring. **A third K8 recurrence found and fixed, not just noted:** `/tmp/phase3/` — holding both English batches' private answer keys and the Spanish FA arrays — is gone, verified absent this session. Blinded clips and answer keys now live in `.listening-clips/`/`.answer-keys/` (gitignored, but outside `/tmp`) going forward.

**Step R — production windowing design, specified, not implemented.** The governing change: alignment moves from per-SEGMENT windows to per-RUN windows, where a run is a maximal group bounded by anchors with **three-source agreement** (Hirschberg match + Whisper token onset + a real detected silence, all within 150ms) on a **distinctive** word inside a **≥4-word matched run** (reusing the shipped run-survival constant, not a new one). Padding is bounded (`PAD_BASE=0.75s`, derived from the corpus's own real silence durations) and clamped at 50% of the gap to the neighbour's own **verified word end** — not its committed boundary, which is the exact defect in today's design (a mistimed neighbour poisons the next window). A mistimed segment structurally cannot become an anchor, so it can't propagate: it's absorbed into the run and re-derived from FA's own output instead. Unscripted audio (headings) gets a CTC wildcard that claims zero alignment cost and belongs to no segment — where those seconds land is flagged as an open owner ruling, not decided here. Corpus start/end get symmetric wildcard + clamp-to-edge handling, aimed directly at V6 segment 1's edge-of-corpus FA anomaly. Cascade-safety argument stated at the strength it holds, not overclaimed: **full independence proven for cross-run neighbours and skipped segments; within a run, reduced from today's verbatim-error-copying to a bounded monotonic-ordering constraint** — not zero. Named case-by-case against Phase 3: prevents the 5 Blocker-2 starvation cases, segment 96's window-construction defect, and segment 1's edge case; partially fixes the 10 headings (removes the arbitrariness, doesn't decide the split) and segments 307/383 (kills the reference error, segment 307's own 335ms FA residual is untouched, per Step G); does not and cannot fix `seasons than you || can count and` (a script-vs-narration authority conflict) or the flash-attention dropout. **A correction found while building this: segment 320's "4.5x undercount" is a stale, pre-Phase-2a artifact** — Step M's own golden baseline shows it's committed today at 974.26-980.17s (5.91s), a correct fit, and segment 321 starts within 270ms of its true onset. The defect is real and R.7's CTC-fit precheck is still required, but it is **latent, not live**.

**Step S — all 12 structural checks built in a standalone harness (`scripts/phase4-step-s-structural-checks.py`), outside the app, no `src/` import.** **13/13 poison cases trip (100%)** — including C12's, which is deliberately *healthy* 20ms-noise data, proving the negative-smear gate itself is the defect, not the pipeline. **Against the three real corpora: 8 of 12 clean or exact, 4 honestly reported as not passing requirement 2** — C05 (short-trailing-word scorer check) can't be validated at all without the FA token arrays that were in the now-gone `/tmp/phase3/`, and 59-100% of its real-corpus flags are actually whisper's gapless-span mechanism, a different defect than the one it targets; C10 (seam cross-attribution) dropped from 29 false positives to 1 after requiring seam words to be phonetically distinctive, but still catches 0 of the 3 known word-shift residuals — explicitly not production-ready; C11 (lock preservation) isn't runnable against real baselines by construction (locks are cleared by resync, K13); C12 correctly rejects all three real projects, which is the expected finding, not a failure. **Segment 320, scored against each of the 12:** only **C01** (implausible chars/sec — 80.3 vs. a 40.0 ceiling derived from the real corpora's own 28.2 max) and **C09** (CTC targets exceed available frames) catch it, each with a single finding across 447 stale-corpus segments and both landing exactly on segment 320. Zero of the 12 catch the segment-321 cascade directly — the defence is C01/C09 catching 320 first, plus Step R's run structure removing the propagation path. Full findings: `docs/measurements/phase4-step-s-check-results.csv` (198 rows).

**Step T — model-distribution design, no Rust.** Total footprint if all 5 languages are installed: **≈7.4 GiB** (1.51 GiB Whisper + 5×1.18 GiB FA) against a ~100-150MB installer budget — **everything downloads on demand; `tauri.conf.json`'s current `models/*` glob-bundle must be removed, a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.** Cache in `app_local_data_dir()` (never `~/Library/Caches`, which macOS can purge; never Windows roaming `%APPDATA%`), a `manifest.json` as the sole source of truth for "installed," SHA-256 pinned in a build-time Rust constant table (never fetched alongside the payload), resumable range-request downloads with a 200-vs-206 detection rule (silently appending to a non-range response corrupts the file). No automatic eviction while any project needs a language; opt-in "keep last N" is OFF by default. Three manual-ingestion paths (file picker, drag-drop, Downloads auto-detect) all funnel through one verify-then-install code path. **Eight failure modes specified**, each with a concrete app behavior — offline (project stays fully usable, only sync gated), interrupted download, no-resume server, insufficient disk, corrupted/tampered file, manual-file checksum mismatch, model missing at project open, two languages open at once (at most one FA model loaded in memory — Step P's own 3.19-4.01 GiB peak-RSS finding makes two simultaneous loads a real risk, not a theoretical one). fr/de/pt marked **UNVALIDATED** on three separate user-facing surfaces (dropdown label, one-time dialog, a new informational `unvalidated-language` sync-log entry type, deliberately distinct from the existing error-severity `unsupported-language` guard).

**What remained before Rust could start, as of this entry:** Step Q's clips needed the owner's ear before Spanish's gate question resolved either way; Step R's one open call (where the heading wildcard's seconds go) needed an owner ruling before Stage 4 finalization could implement it; C05/C10/C11 needed either the recovered FA arrays, an ear-verified word-shift corpus, or a live K13 repro before they'd be trustworthy enough to wire into CI. None of the six owner decisions was contradicted by anything found in this pass — decision 3 (jonatasgrosman, all 5 languages) stands, decision 1 (250ms gate) stands with Spanish's pass/fail still open exactly as flagged, decisions 4-7 are what Steps R/S/T executed against. The one genuine update was factual, not decisional: segment 320 is confirmed latent rather than live under the shipped-at-the-time pipeline.
